candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: obtain specimens using appropriate infection-related procedures and support timely evidence-based management of suspected infection.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — culture collection and antimicrobial sequencing in sepsis
candidate.educational_objective: In suspected adult sepsis, obtain blood cultures promptly and ideally before antimicrobials while ensuring that diagnostic sampling does not create avoidable delay in emergency treatment; use resulting microbiology to refine therapy.

options.A: Collect the blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before the first antimicrobial dose, while avoiding unnecessary delay of emergency sepsis treatment.
options.B: Delay antimicrobial therapy until final blood-culture identification and susceptibility results are available.
options.C: Give the first antimicrobial dose before collecting blood cultures because prior antibiotic exposure improves culture yield.
options.D: Cancel the blood cultures once empiric antibiotics are ordered because culture results no longer affect treatment decisions.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign adult guideline recommends collecting blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before antimicrobial therapy in adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock. The same guideline emphasizes that sepsis and septic shock are medical emergencies and treatment and resuscitation should begin immediately. B is unsafe because definitive culture results are not required before empiric treatment when sepsis warrants antimicrobials. C reverses the recommended order and antibiotic exposure can reduce microbiologic recovery. D is incorrect because microbiologic diagnosis and susceptibility results support later antimicrobial de-escalation or narrowing.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For adults with suspected or confirmed sepsis, blood cultures should be collected promptly and ideally before antimicrobials, without allowing diagnostic sampling to undermine immediate emergency management; microbiology should later guide de-escalation.
candidate.source_document_title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026
candidate.source_locator: Diagnostics — Blood culture recommendation: for adults with possible, probable, or definite sepsis or septic shock, collect blood cultures as soon as possible and ideally before administration of antimicrobial therapy. Fluid resuscitation/initial management good-practice statement: sepsis and septic shock are medical emergencies and treatment/resuscitation should begin immediately. Antimicrobial therapy: de-escalate/narrow therapy when microbiological diagnosis and susceptibility profile are available.
candidate.source_organization: Society of Critical Care Medicine / European Society of Intensive Care Medicine, Surviving Sepsis Campaign
